identity.name: GRAVITA INDIA LIMITED
identity.industry: Metals Recycling & Circular Economy / Lead, Copper & EV Battery Recycling

summary.oneLiner: Gravita significantly expanded its footprint beyond lead with the RML acquisition and copper recycling capex, driving a structural shift toward higher-margin value-added copper and EV battery recycling; despite Q4 EBITDA pressure from West Asia logistics and aluminum/plastic hedging delays, the company is on track for 20-25% volume CAGR through FY29 with 20%+ ROCE expected from integrated copper operations.

one-line thesis: Gravita significantly expanded its footprint beyond lead with the RML acquisition and copper recycling capex, driving a structural shift toward higher-margin value-added copper and EV battery recycling; despite Q4 EBITDA pressure from West Asia logistics and aluminum/plastic hedging delays, the company is on track for 20-25% volume CAGR through FY29 with 20%+ ROCE expected from integrated copper operations.
financial scorecard: revenue: +10% YoY (FY26: ₹4,265cr); EBITDA/margin: +12% YoY, 10.6% margin (FY26); PAT (rptd): +21% YoY (₹378.8cr); PAT (normalized): +21% YoY (no major one-offs); order book: not disclosed; net debt: ₹118cr (pre-copper), expected to rise to ₹700-800cr post-copper capex and working capital build
guidance: revenue growth: 20-25% CAGR volume through FY29; margin: copper EBITDA/ton to rise from ₹45k to ₹60-65k; order inflow: not specified; capex/commissioning: ₹1,700cr total through FY29 (₹700cr copper, ₹160cr Mandvi copper recycling, ₹14cr Li-ion pilot, ₹49cr Mundra lead expansion); commissioning: copper recycling (Mandvi) in 12 months, Li-ion scaling in FY27, lead expansion (Jaipur) in Q1FY27
segment / subsidiary detail: Lead: 48,889 tons sold (+7% YoY), EBITDA/ton ₹23,043; Copper: RML acquired (31,200 tons capacity), EBITDA/ton ₹45,000, targeting ₹60,000-65,000 post-backward integration; Lithium-ion: 6,000 tons/year pilot commissioned (Jan’26); Aluminum: EBITDA/ton ₹16,043 (sustainable target ₹14,000-15,000), growth delayed pending MCX hedging; Plastic: EBITDA/ton ₹12,328 (sustainable ₹10,000-12,000); Rubber: 30,000 tons/year capacity planned (H1FY27), EBITDA/ton ₹7,000-8,000
growth verticals / optionality: Copper recycling (100,000 tons by FY29); Lithium-ion scaling; Rubber recycling (India + Romania); Steel recycling (long-term, post FY29); Value-added alloy expansion via RML
margins & cost dynamics: Lead: ₹19,000-20,000/ton sustainable (Q4 pressured by West Asia); Copper: ₹45,000/ton (RML), targeting ₹60,000-65,000 with recycling integration; Aluminum: ₹14,000-15,000/ton (current ₹16,043 due to price surge); Plastic: ₹10,000-12,000/ton; Rubber: ₹7,000-8,000/ton; Cost headwinds: elevated logistics from West Asia disruption, copper import costs
capex / expansion: ₹1,700cr total through FY29: ₹700cr copper (₹160cr Mandvi recycling + ₹540cr RML integration/expansion), ₹49cr Mundra lead expansion, ₹14cr Li-ion pilot, ₹815cr total for existing biz, ₹885cr for new verticals (Cu, Li-ion, rubber, steel)
capital allocation: 100% internally funded capex; working capital debt expected ₹700-900cr (metal-backed, hedged); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on recycling verticals over shareholder returns
risks & watch-items: West Asia logistics disruption (10-12% of sales); MCX aluminum hedging delay (impacting Al growth); copper import supply chain risks; integration execution risk with RML; regulatory delays in EPR compliance; commodity price volatility
management quality / tone: Confident, strategic, and execution-focused; emphasized disciplined capex, backward integration, and long-term CAGR targets; acknowledged near-term headwinds (West Asia, hedging) but framed them as temporary; tone bullish on copper and EV recycling as structural growth drivers
non-obvious takeaways: Copper EBITDA/ton target of ₹65,000 implies >40% margin expansion from RML’s current ₹45,000 — driven by scrap sourcing synergy and value-added product mix, not just recycling; working capital debt is treated as ‘hedged metal inventory’ not traditional debt — a key accounting nuance; aluminum/plastic margins are intentionally suppressed until MCX hedging enables scale — a deliberate capital preservation strategy
